claim.why_it_matters: Flowchart flattened to labels; the branch-to-outcome connections are lost and the outcomes rendered as a table.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 891 (printed 867) shows the Figure D.8 flowchart: Evaluate condition-1/2/n boxes alternating with 'Condition-k true' decision ovals; each 'yes' exits right into a single vertical line arrowed down to 'Truth value is true'; each 'no' continues down to the next evaluation, and the last 'no' arrows to 'Truth value is false'. The markdown keeps only the box and label text in sequence ('Condition-1 yes\ true', 'no', ...) and ends with a two-column table 'Truth value | Truth value / is false | is true'. No edge information survives: nothing in the markdown says that any 'yes' leads to true or that only the final 'no' leads to false, and the table falsely presents the two outcomes as a header/data grid. The edges are the figure's entire content (OR short-circuit evaluation), so this is a genuine content loss, not mere formatting. The Figure D.7 caption at the top of the markdown is faithful (the PDF page carries that caption above this figure too), so it is not part of the defect. Informative Annex D figure, so structural rather than normative. Claim is accurately described.
